title: fix(codex): recover failed conversations while sibling work continues
body:
Fixes #172279. Follow-up to #149000.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated Codex conversation recovery failures after a provider error when another thread keeps the shared app-server active.

## User Impact

A failed conversation can resume its original thread and history with refreshed instructions while sibling work continues. Healthy conversations also wait for asynchronous teardown before resuming. User-owned Codex homes and external proxy/socket connections retain their native retention settings. Provider rate limits still apply.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw already owns warm subscription retention and child-work protection. Managed local agent-home app-servers now launch with `thread_unload_delay_secs=0`. The lifecycle owner waits for the matching `notLoaded` notification for up to two seconds, aborting with the run. Missing confirmation preserves the binding; the existing guarded whole-client replacement remains available for settled failures only when no sibling work would be interrupted.

Original fix by @zhuyankarl; maintainer cleanup coordinates healthy-thread teardown, preserves external connection behavior, replaces the expensive new native test with focused lifecycle cases, and updates the existing Gateway recovery controls.

## Evidence

PR CI is the test and typecheck gate per maintainer policy. Live proof, local tests, local typechecks, and production-revert negative controls were intentionally skipped. No local Gateway or remote lease was started. The first exact-head run [38683475836](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38683475836) exposed fixture typing, stale managed-unload state, and replacement-clock failures. Those PR-caused failures are corrected in the follow-up commit; no inherited-failure exception is claimed. Final-head [CI run 38684859899, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38684859899/attempts/2), head `76dca1a1833811b94c600216cd1176347523c256`: **37 jobs passed**, including production/test typechecks, lint, and the affected extension suites. Four affected test shards passed **663 tests across 36 files** (122 binding/lifecycle, 134 auth/startup, 193 run-attempt, 214 extension tests).

**CI infrastructure blocker:** three jobs still failed in **Set up job**, before checkout or test execution, because GitHub could not download `actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e` (HTTP 404): [changed tests, job 116260133227](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38684859899/job/116260133227), [Gateway, job 116260133434](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38684859899/job/116260133434), and [compact-large-13, job 116260133501](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38684859899/job/116260133501). One diagnosed infrastructure retry used the workflow's supported GitHub-hosted fallback; these three downloads still failed. The aggregate gate remains red, so this PR is **not yet land-ready**. No inherited code-failure exception or maintainer acceptance is claimed.

- Regression: `preserves managed $nativeStatus history across $outcome with sibling=$sibling` in the existing `thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts` suite: failed/healthy unload, unrelated notification rejection, timeout with/without sibling protection, and abort. Uses the real RPC client/lifecycle with synthetic responses and fake timers.
- Launch contract: `owns unload retention only for managed local starts: $transport/$homeScope/proxy=$proxy` in `auth-bridge.test.ts`, including explicit native retention settings and user-home/proxy/WebSocket/Unix exclusions.
- Existing Gateway composition `server.codex-failure-recovery.test.ts` now expects same-thread/same-client recovery, changed instructions, preserved history, and sibling completion. Replacement/cancellation/unconfirmed-exit controls explicitly retain the native cache; no serial config or worker pin was added.
- Removed the contributor's 299-line native test and lane registration. Its original reported cost was 3.435 seconds per case and 193.79 seconds cold wrapper time; those prior-head results are not current proof. The existing Gateway composition remains optional native validation. Final-head CI measured the six new regression cases at 112/87/102/103/89/145 ms (0.638 seconds combined), the five launch-scope cases at 0.049 seconds combined, and the replacement controls at 377/327 ms. The existing real Gateway cases passed for active-sibling recovery (21.005s), healthy reload (7.743s), idle Incognito (7.274s), and idle persistent siblings (6.421s). Those four native Gateway results are from the prior head; the final-head Gateway job never started because of the action download failure above. Dedicated live proof and a production-revert negative control were not run.
- Changed-file `oxfmt` and static `oxlint` passed. Lint ran from clean trusted main using its rules with only the nonmatching `ui/**/*.tsx` Solid-plugin override omitted because that unrelated dependency is absent. No install was run. `git diff --check` passed.
- Deslop removed redundant synchronous rechecks and obsolete native-test setup. Isolated Codex autoreview at P2: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable findings; the final test-only CI repair received a separate scoped-clean review. The required main merge was conflict-free and changed none of the reviewed owner/test files or supplied source context.

### Native dependency contract

Personally inspected the sibling Codex source at [`rust-v0.160.0`, commit a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc), matching the plugin's `@openai/codex` `0.160.0` pin:

- [`core/src/config/mod.rs:3911–3919`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs#L3911-L3919) reads `thread_unload_delay_secs`; the release default is **60 seconds**, correcting the issue's 1,800-second description. Zero is supported.
- [`thread_processor.rs:4336–4385`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L4336-L4385) reloads changed overrides only with no subscribers, `Idle`, and no running agent; settled `SystemError` does not qualify. [`3650–3659`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L3650-L3659) rejects a thread whose asynchronous unload is pending.
- [`thread_lifecycle.rs:363–394`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs#L363-L394) schedules idle unsubscribe teardown; [`434–457`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_lifecycle.rs#L434-L457) awaits shutdown and removes the thread. [`thread_status.rs:333–347`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_status.rs#L333-L347) produces the exact-thread `notLoaded` notification, emitted at [`242–247`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_status.rs#L242-L247).

### Review decisions and scope

ClawSweeper's healthy teardown P1 and outdated Gateway controls P2 are addressed above. Its additional live-proof asks are intentionally deferred: PR CI is the proof per maintainer policy. The managed-server retention policy is the requested fix scope; it adds no OpenClaw option and excludes user-home/external ownership. No separate approval is claimed.

The wait captures the exact physical client, thread ID, binding lease, and initial native status. Current host/run/client authority is checked after the wait and before native writes; the binding remains serialized by its existing owner. Replacement eligibility reads current leases, pending acquisitions, sibling claims, and routes after waiting. Configuration is built after the wait or remains bound to the current turn's existing preparation authority. There is no detached recovery task, new path, or new retention store.

Production is net +57 lines versus main: the bounded notification/abort handoff and shared launch-scope rule need these additions; no unrelated deletion is used to meet the campaign LOC target. Final numstat: production **+60/−3 (net +57)**, tests **+239/−85 (net +154)**, docs **+10/−0 (net +10)**; total **+309/−88 (net +221)** across 13 files. Compared with the contributor patch, maintainer cleanup removes 142 lines overall.
